subject: Skyline pilot — success matrix, GPU reservation, and surge policy
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@skylinesystems.com>, pilot@skylinesystems.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Skyline pilot — success matrix, GPU reservation, and surge policy

Hi Liam / Skyline team,

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation. Per our call, here is a concise post-call recap and the concrete asks so we can lock the pilot schedule by EoW. I've attached a short one-pager (pilot scope) and our autoscale appendix.

1) Success criteria (what Skyline will measure)
- Functional: feature parity for batch routing and tokenization with your on-prem baseline (no more than 2% semantic drift on the 400-sample slice).
- Performance: 95th percentile response latency <= 220ms on the production prompt set (avg prompt length ~350 tokens) during baseline load.
- Throughput: sustained 1,000 queries/day with peaks up to 12 QPS for short windows (burst).
- Cost / ops: predictable unit cost within agreed pilot budget; artifacts for SOC2 scoping provided.

2) Proposed evaluation plan (week-by-week)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope & NDAs; exchange test prompts + sample dataset (you to share).
- Week 1: provisioning + model onboarding + smoke tests (internal Redwood).
- Week 2: controlled eval — run curated prompt set (1k prompts) and collect metrics (latency, tokens, mem pressure).
- Week 3: integration testing with Skyline routing + UX; iterate on prompt templates.
- Week 4: acceptance window; handoff notes and go/no-go.

3) Capacity proposal (initial commitment + burst plan)
- Baseline (reserved for pilot): 2 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved), pinned for the 4-week pilot window. This should cover steady usage and KV cache warm-up.
- Autoscale / burst: autoscale pool up to 8 GPUs for short bursts. We will enforce a warm-start policy for burst (pre-warm containers for additional GPUs within a 3–5 minute window) to minimize cold-start latency.
- Expected throughput per GPU (approx): 60–80 short-interactive RPS for ~350-token prompts (this is workload-dependent; we'll run a baseline perf test in Week 1).
- Fallbacks: if burst capacity is unavailable, requests will route to a compatible quantized model variant (slightly lower quality) — we'll surface this in tracing/console and add a business-rule toggle accessible to your SREs.

4) Ownership / next steps
- Redwood owner: Jonas Weber (pilot lead) — overall schedule, infra reservations, and billing alignment.
- Solution & onboarding: Karthik Iyer — model/SDK integration and evaluation harness.
- Customer success contact: Marissa Cole — acceptance criteria and success metrics.

Please confirm these items (scope, baseline GPUs, and acceptance timeline) or suggest edits. If you confirm by Friday (2026-10-16), we can have baseline GPUs reserved and a test cluster ready by Monday (2026-10-19).

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@skylinesystems.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: pilot@skylinesystems.com
Date: 2026-10-12T17:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline pilot — success matrix, GPU reservation, and surge policy

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick points/questions: 

1) The success latency target looks ok, although we may push for 180ms 95p if the model variant keeps quality parity. Is that something you can commit to in the Week 2 run?
2) On the autoscale: can you confirm what the billing model for bursts looks like (pay-as-you-go vs committed burst credit)? We have a tight ops budget for Q4.
3) SOC2 evidence — can you attach the evidence snapshot we can share with our security team?

I'll loop in our infra lead if we look to accelerate. For timeline, Friday sign-off is reasonable if we have the SOC2 snapshot and a rough burst pricing figure.

— Liam
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@skylinesystems.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline pilot — success matrix, GPU reservation, and surge policy

Liam — quick answers inline.

> 1) The success latency target looks ok, although we may push for 180ms 95p if the model variant keeps quality parity. Is that something you can commit to in the Week 2 run?
We can't universally commit to 180ms 95p without running the Week 1 perf profile because latency is sensitive to prompt length and KV cache hit rate. That said, for the model family you indicated on the call (redwood-rlm-1-small-quant), we typically see 95p in the 160–210ms range for 256–512 token prompts on A100-80GB with warm KV cache. We will run a controlled benchmark in Week 1 and produce a latency/quality tradeoff matrix.

> 2) On the autoscale: can you confirm what the billing model for bursts looks like (pay-as-you-go vs committed burst credit)?
Pilot billing options:
- Option A (pay-as-you-go): burst GPUs billed at on-demand rate per GPU-hour, no upfront commit.
- Option B (burst credit): commit to a small burst credit (e.g., 100 GPU-hours) at a discounted rate applied to the pilot invoice; unused hours roll over for 30 days.
We'll include both options in the pilot SOW so Skyline can pick. For Q4 budget constraints, Option B is usually easier to forecast.

> 3) SOC2 evidence — can you attach the evidence snapshot we can share with our security team?
Attaching 'SOC2-excerpt.pdf' (redwood redacted). That includes our control attestations and where to find logs for pilot-level audit. If you need an IP-protected artifact or NDA'd evidence, we can route it through your security channel.

Operational note: to guarantee burst warm-start behavior, we'll reserve a thin pre-warm pool (1–2 standby containers) so the 3–5 minute warm-up is deterministic — we'll call this out in the SOW.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@skylinesystems.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline pilot — success matrix, GPU reservation, and surge policy

Liam — thanks, pushed a tightened acceptance bullet into the doc: we'll target 180ms 95p as an aspirational target and surface the Week 1 results so you can decide if it's achievable for your prompt distribution.

Attached: updated pilot-scope.pdf (minor edits), redwood-autoscale-policy-appendix.txt.

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm choice between burst billing Option A or B by Friday 2026-10-16.
- Skyline shares sample prompt corpus and the dev service account for integration (pilot@skylinesystems.com to provide a service key).
- Redwood reserves the baseline 2x A100-equivalent GPUs on receipt of a signed pilot SOW (sample SOW attached).

I've cc'd Marissa to prepare the SOW template and Marissa / Karthik will join the kickoff call once sign-off is in.

Jonas
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@skylinesystems.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: pilot@skylinesystems.com
Date: 2026-10-15T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline pilot — success matrix, GPU reservation, and surge policy

Jonas / Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the speedy follow-up. We reviewed the attachments and options.

- We'll go with Option B (burst credit) and propose an initial 120 GPU-hours of burst credit for the pilot.
- We'll share the prompt corpus and a service account by EOD Friday (2026-10-16).
- SOC2 excerpt looks good for initial review; our security lead may request one targeted control artifact during Week 2.

Please proceed to prepare the SOW with Option B and the baseline 2x A100 reservation. If you can circulate a calendar invite for the kickoff early next week, we'll lock the pilot dates.

— Liam
